articles.title: Deezer says AI song uploads have nearly overtaken human music
articles.summary: Deezer says it receives almost 75,000 AI-generated song submissions to its music streaming platform each day, which accounts for about 44 percent of all daily uploads.
articles.body: Deezer says it receives nearly 75,000 AI-generated song submissions to its music streaming platform each day, accounting for about 44 percent of all daily uploads, as reported earlier by TechCrunch. Despite the increase in “fraudulent” uploads, Deezer says the consumption of AI songs makes up around 1 to 3 percent of total streams, as the platform continues to remove AI-generated music from its recommendation algorithm. Deezer positions the tool as setting an “industry standard,” adding that the platform is currently the “only” music streaming service tagging AI-generated tracks. The service also demonetizes AI-generated songs and has stopped storing high-resolution versions of them. “AI-generated music is now far from a marginal phenomenon and as daily deliveries keep increasing, we hope the whole music ecosystem will join us in taking action to help safeguard artist’s rights and promote transparency for fans,” Deezer CEO Alexis Lanternier writes in the blog post. As AI-powered song-making tools like Suno and Udio become more popular, music streaming services are dealing with the flood of AI tracks in different ways. While Spotify announced new policies to clamp down on AI-generated music, Apple Music is asking artists and record labels to label songs made with AI. Bandcamp has banned AI music altogether, while Qobuz has started automatically detecting and labeling AI music as well. Since launching its tool in January 2025, Deezer says the number of AI-generated tracks uploaded daily has jumped from 10,000 to 75,000. Deezer has also started allowing other companies to license its AI song-detecting tool. As noted by Deezer, the tool can identify songs made using Udio and Suno, “with the possibility to add detection capabilities for practically any other similar tool as long as there’s access to relevant data examples.” The company is also working on a way for its music detection tool to identify songs without requiring a dataset to train on.

articles.title: Billionaire Michael Dell breaks his silence after wife Susan's controversial White House appearance
articles.summary: Michael Dell has rallied behind his wife Susan after trolls mocked her White House appearance, sharing supportive messages and children's thank-you letters.
articles.body:
Michael Del l has shown his support for his wife Susan after she became the subject of debate following their recent White House appearance.

The technology billionaire , 61, shared messages defending Susan, 62, after photographs and footage of the couple's visit prompted personal remarks about her looks.

The pair had travelled to Washington to discuss their $6.25 billion pledge to children's investment accounts. But as clips circulated online, attention turned to Susan's appearance, prompting supporters to speak out and Michael to amplify their words.

Michael Dell shares messages defending wife Susan

Michael shared posts from people urging others to leave his wife alone, including parents and grandparents who said their families had benefited from the couple's contribution.

One supporter described discovering that both of their sons had received $250 and said the gesture had inspired them to support the Dells.

Another wrote: "My grandson got 250 dollars in his Trump account from Susan Dell. Please leave that woman alone."

"The Dell family gave 7 billion dollars directly to American children. And instead of gratitude, there's much discussion of a 62 year old woman's looks," conservative Mike Cernovich wrote on X.

Michael shared the supportive messages and responded with emojis expressing thanks. His response came through those posts, rather than a lengthy personal statement addressing the criticism.

Eric Trump also defended the couple on X, condemning the attacks and pointing to the scale of their charitable commitment.

Michael subsequently shared children's thank-you letters, bringing attention back to the young people the initiative was designed to help. HELLO! reached out to Michael's reps for comment.

Susan and Michael appeared in the Oval Office on Wednesday, 7 October, to discuss their contribution to Trump Accounts.

Their pledge, announced in December 2025, was intended to provide $250 each for 25 million children. At the event, Michael said 10 million accounts had been funded, with the remainder expected by the end of that week.

Susan spoke about letters from children, parents and grandparents that had moved the couple. Some young recipients, she explained, hoped to become nurses, doctors, engineers or start businesses of their own.

She also described the importance of children knowing that someone believed in their future, alongside the financial contribution itself.

Michael and Susan Dell's 37-year marriage

The couple's public appearance came shortly before their 37th wedding anniversary.

They met on a blind date in Austin in February 1988 and married in October 1989. Together, they have four children: daughters Alexa, Kira and Juliette, and son Zachary.

Susan has built her own career alongside her husband's technology business, founding three fashion labels, including luxury brand Phi. An accomplished athlete, she has also competed in marathons, triathlons and the Ironman World Championships in Hawaii.

The couple established the Michael & Susan Dell Foundation in 1999, with Susan serving as chair and helping guide its work in education, healthcare and support for families.

On their official website, Susan explains the commitment behind their philanthropy: "We believe giving is the most important thing we will do in our lives."

articles.title: Festival de Artes Cênicas Preta do Maranhão reúne teatro, dança e performances em São Luís | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento ocorre de 13 a 17 de outubro, com espetáculos, oficinas, performances, lançamentos de livros e atividades em diferentes espaços da capital.
articles.summary: Evento ocorre de 13 a 17 de outubro, com espetáculos, oficinas, performances, lançamentos de livros e atividades em diferentes espaços da capital.
articles.body:
O Festival de Artes Cênicas Preta do Maranhão será realizado de 13 a 17 de outubro de 2026, em São Luís , com uma programação de teatro, dança, performances, oficinas e lançamentos de livros. As atividades serão distribuídas por espaços culturais, teatros, escolas e pontos do Centro Histórico da capital.

A programação começa nesta terça-feira (13), com oficinas, cenas curtas, a abertura oficial do festival e o espetáculo Língua de Boi, da Cia Maranhense, às 20h, no Teatro Sesc Napoleão Ewerton. A apresentação tem classificação indicativa de 12 anos e interpretação em Língua Brasileira de Sinais (Libras).

Na quarta-feira (14) , o público poderá acompanhar espetáculos e performances em diferentes espaços. Entre os destaques estão Flor de Mulungu, do Coletivo Mulungu, às 16h, no Teatro Sesc Napoleão Ewerton, com audiodescrição e interpretação em Libras, e Mover-se como Plantas, da Plataforma Gang, às 19h30, no Teatro Luiz Pazzini.

Na quinta-feira (15) , a programação inclui a performance Cuidado com Nós, às 10h, na Rua Grande, e À Sombra da Goiabeira, do grupo Teatro Negro e Atitude, de Minas Gerais, às 19h30, no Teatro Luiz Pazzini. Também haverá oficinas e outras performances ao longo do dia.

Na sexta-feira (16) , estão previstos um roteiro afroturístico pelo Centro Histórico, às 15h, o lançamento de livros, às 16h, e a performance Yarara Xaxará, de Tiyê Macau, às 18h, no Espaço Cultural Humberto de Maracanã. Às 20h, o Teatro Luiz Pazzini recebe o espetáculo de dança Malemole, de Déborah Santos e Jônatas Joca, do Ceará.

O encerramento será no sábado (17) , com espetáculos em diferentes horários. Às 16h, o Teatro Luiz Pazzini recebe O Tiro, de Luiz Lucas, de Minas Gerais. Às 17h, será apresentado Histórias na Terra, de Kamylla dos Santos, do Grupo Baquetá, do Paraná, no Centro Cultural Vale Maranhão. Às 19h, o Teatro Arthur Azevedo recebe Parto Pavilhão, com Aysha Nascimento, direção de Naruna Costa e texto de Jhonny Salaberg. A apresentação tem classificação indicativa de 14 anos e interpretação em Libras.

Além dos espetáculos, a programação inclui oficinas de teatro, dança, dramaturgia e produção cultural. Entre os temas estão estética da atitude e poética da negrura, jogos de presença e criação, dança e ancestralidade, além de produção e gestão para negócios criativos.

Parte das oficinas será realizada em escolas parceiras e terá acesso restrito aos participantes dessas instituições. O festival também prevê atividades de mediação nas escolas que receberão as cenas curtas.

articles.title: Voz etérea de 'Teletema', Regininha deixa álbum gravado com a Turma da Pilantragem e música na discografia de Roberto Carlos ao morrer aos 81 anos | G1
articles.body:
Regininha (1945 – 2026), cantora falecida aos 81 anos, teve música gravada por Roberto Carlos em 1981 — Foto: Reprodução / Capa do álbum 'Me ajuda que a voz não dá!!' (1969)

♬ Em outubro de 1981, há 45 anos, Roberto Carlos estava em estúdio para gravar o álbum que lançaria em 26 de novembro daquele ano de 1981. Uma das músicas era “Simples mágica”, composição de Regininha, artista que trabalhava como vocalista e colaborava com grandes nomes da música brasileira, inclusive Roberto Carlos.

Regininha era o nome artístico de Regina Amália Serra de Souza (1º de outubro de 1945 – 13 de outubro de 2026), cantora e compositora carioca falecida hoje, aos 81 anos, de causa não revelada.

“Simples mágica” não era uma música inédita quando foi gravada por Roberto Carlos. A própria Regininha já gravara a música em EP lançado em 1979 com ficha técnica que creditava a autoria de “Simples mágica” a Regininha, Jamil Joanes e Ronaldo Monteiro.

Contudo, “Simples mágica” é música que logo seria esquecida com o passar dos anos. Para o público, Regininha fica imortalizada como a voz etérea da gravação da canção “Teletema” (1969), uma das músicas mais conhecidas da parceria de Antonio Adolfo com Tibério Gaspar (1943 – 2017). “Teletema” foi o principal tema da trilha sonora da novela “Véu de noiva”, exibida pela TV Globo de outubro de 1969 a junho de 1970 com grande sucesso.

Ainda em 1969, ano áureo da trajetória profissional iniciada por Regininha no fim de 1966 como integrante do coletivo Musicanossa (movimento criado para dar foco à bossa nova, então desvalorizada no Brasil), a cantora lançou o que se tornaria o único álbum da discografia.

Embora gravado com A Turma da Pilantragem, como creditado na capa, “Me ajuda que a voz não dá!!” (1969) pode ser considerado um álbum solo de Regininha. O título vem do inusitado pedido de socorro feito por Regininha enquanto gravava a música “Primavera” (Carlos Lyra e Vinicius de Moraes, 1964).

Além de “Primavera”, a cantora pôs voz em músicas como “Tem dó” (Baden Powell e Vinicius de Moraes, 1963) e “Deixa a nega gingar” (Luiz Cláudio de Castro, 1960) com o suingue da Turma da Pilantragem.

Na sequência, em 1970, Regininha formou o trio vocal Umas e Outras com Dorinha Tapajós e Malu Balona, se dedicando posteriormente ao trabalho como vocalista e como cantora de jingles. Contudo, Regininha jamais foi esquecida pela gravação antológica de “Teletema”, música que deixa a cantora eternizada na história da música brasileira.

articles.title: MT recebe Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia com oficinas de IA | G1
articles.standfirst: Programação gratuita inclui atividades sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e participação das mulheres na ciência.
articles.summary: Programação gratuita inclui atividades sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e participação das mulheres na ciência.
articles.body:
Mato Grosso recebe, entre os dias 21 e 23 de outubro, a 23ª edição da Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (SNCT). — Foto: Secom-MT

Mato Grosso recebe, entre os dias 21 e 23 de outubro, a 23ª edição da Semana Nacional de Ciência e Tecnologia (SNCT), com palestras, oficinas e atividades gratuitas sobre inteligência artificial, robótica, sustentabilidade e inovação. O evento será realizado no Centro de Eventos do Pantanal, em Cuiabá , e é aberto a estudantes, professores, pesquisadores e demais interessados. As inscrições podem ser feitas pela página oficial do evento .

A programação inclui debates sobre o uso da tecnologia na saúde, a participação das mulheres na ciência, a preparação dos jovens para o mercado de trabalho e a educação climática. Os interessados podem fazer a inscrição para palestras específicas no site.

Promovido pela Secretaria de Estado de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (Seciteci-MT), o evento também reúne a 18ª Mostra Estadual de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação (MECTI) , o 2º Festival Estadual High Tech – Tecnologia, Indústria e Cultura Digital e o 1º Hack Festival Estadual .

A abertura oficial será na quarta-feira (21), às 9h. No primeiro dia, as atividades incluem palestras sobre mercado de trabalho, participação de meninas na tecnologia e proteção de invenções.

Na quinta-feira (22), a programação terá palestras sobre a presença feminina nas áreas científicas e tecnológicas, além de oficinas práticas de inteligência artificial, robótica e sustentabilidade.

Já na sexta-feira (23), os participantes poderão acompanhar atividades sobre agricultura, mudanças climáticas, pesquisa científica e uso de dados na saúde. O evento também terá a premiação dos projetos apresentados na 18ª Mostra Estadual de Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, às 15h.

articles.title: Danny Trejo’s Son Claims Actor “Never Heard” Of Ben Shapiro Until 2 Weeks Into ICE Film Production: “He’s Handcuffed To This Stupid Project”
articles.summary: As Danny Trejo is met with backlash over his involvement in Daily Wire’s latest project, his son is coming to the actor’s defense. This weekend, Gilbert Trej...
articles.body:
As Danny Trejo is met with backlash over his involvement in Daily Wire's latest project, his son is coming to the actor's defense.

This weekend, Gilbert Trejo claimed that his father had "never heard of Ben Shapiro" or "what kind of guy he is" until two weeks into production own Daily Wire and Bonfire Legend's Pawn Shop , which has been described as a pro-ICE film that seemingly dramatizes the killing of Renée Good .

"For anyone seeing this shit with my dad…" he begain a statement on his Instagram Story, which was shared by The San Fernando Valley Sun . "He was booked on a film, it's not pro-ICE, it's not overtly pro anything. His agent described it as 'a complicated story about a complicated time, where everyone looks bad except you, the hardworking Mexican shop owner who just wants peace.'

"He jumped at the idea of playing a good guy. About 2 weeks into shooting everyone, including us, found out Ben Shapiro was involved. My 82-year-old dad has never heard of Ben Shapiro, I had to explain to him who that is, and what kind of guy he is. My dad contractually can't bad mouth him, the film, or walk away without being sued for breach of contract. He couldn't even release the statement he wanted to."

Gilbert continued, "It's fucked up. He's handcuffed to this stupid project, and swaths of people have instantly turned their back on him without knowing any of the facts. Ben Shapiro got Mexicans to abandon one of their heroes, got his own name to the top of google's searches, and made us look like angry fools lacking any nuance. He wins."

Last week, Danny Trejo broke his silence following backlash to his role in the movie. "Hey everyone. I want to address some social media comments about me," he said. "Make no mistake. I am a proud Mexican who has always been and will always be a supporter of my community. I am also obviously, pro-immigrant. I am not pro-ICE. I know where I come from and I know our struggles. I am an actor. My job is to tell a story. God Bless you, Danny."

The synopsis for Pawn Shop reads: 'When chaos hits the streets of Minneapolis, a young federal agent is left alone after his partner is seriously hurt and must find a way to survive an increasingly dangerous situation. Seeking shelter inside a neighborhood pawn shop, he becomes trapped with a traditional Hispanic father and his progressive college-age son, forcing three very different men to confront fear, conflicting beliefs and a crisis that tests their courage and humanity."

Since filming began, locals have protested the alleged use of blank gunshots, pyrotechnics and a staged car wreck without properly notifying residents and businesses, as well as its opening scene, which appears to dramatize ICE's fatal shooting of Renée Good in Minnesota back in January.

Production was temporarily suspended earlier this month, resuming with a revised film permit last Tuesday, requiring the crew to ensure food pantry access for locals to the Livingston Food Resource Center, and shielding the public both from the shooting of violent scenes, as well as from noise. The production also agreed to address backlash to their use of private security, ensuring there would be no policing or harassing of locals on nearby public streets.

Shapiro decried the suspension as "a violation of the First Amendment," calling the film's critics "censorious jackasses" who oppose free speech.

articles.title: Selma Blair’s Lawyer Says Alleged Airplane Attacks Were ‘Not Intentional.’ Here’s His Explanation
articles.summary: Blair pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault in Queens Criminal Court
articles.body:
Selma Blair missed doses of medication before allegedly assaulting flight attendants, a police officer and a nurse, her attorney reportedly said

"This was not an intentional assault," attorney Shawn Barnes said, per the New York Post

Blair pleaded not guilty to two counts of assault in Queens and still faces potential federal charges

Selma Blair's attorney reportedly said in court that his client did not intend to assault a police officer and a nurse .

Blair is facing both federal and state charges after she allegedly attacked two flight attendants while on a plane to New York's John F. Kennedy International Airport on Sunday, Oct. 11.

Upon arrival to New York, Blair, who was taken to a hospital, then allegedly kicked a police officer and a nurse, the Associated Press reported.

Per the AP, the New York Post and the New York Daily News , Blair appeared in Queens Criminal Court Monday night, where she pleaded not guilty to charges connected to the alleged assault of the nurse and police officer.

"This was not an intentional assault," Blair's attorney Shawn Barnes said in court, per the Post.

The Post and the Daily News both reported that Barnes claimed Blair had missed several doses of medication and that before she boarded the flight, she had endured a heavy work schedule.

"These factors, coupled with the altitude, resulted in a state of severe confusion and disorientation," Barnes said, according to the Daily News .

Judge Indira Kahn imposed $20,000 cash bail, $60,000 bond or a $60,000 partially secured bond, per court records. Blair was released Monday evening.

PEOPLE previously reported that the Port Authority Police officer whom Blair allegedly kicked was Maria Suarez.

Suarez suffered swelling to her jaw and substantial pain to her face, neck and chest, according to a criminal court affidavit.

Per the affidavit, the nurse reported substantial chest pain after she was allegedly kicked.

PEOPLE previously reported dispatch audio, in which medical responders were asked to meet the flight at the gate after its arrival at JFK after it was reported there were "some minor injuries, a bloody nose as well as some bite marks as well."

A representative for Blair released a statement following the incident.

" Selma experienced a medical emergency that led to the alleged conduct," the representative said. "Upon landing, she received immediate medical attention and is currently in stable condition."

articles.title: Art of Play lists bird at center of Kelly Clarkson feud for $15M | Exclusive
articles.summary: Amid an ongoing feud with Kelly Clarkson, the specialty store Art of Play listed Molly, its custom animatronic bird, for sale for $15 million.
articles.body:
BROOKLYN, N.Y. – Amid an ongoing dispute with Kelly Clarkson , New York City specialty store Art of Play has been met with both backlash and support – and it's responding by listing the animatronic bird at the center of the controversy for sale at a massive markup.

The curiosity shop in Brooklyn has been embroiled in a back-and-forth with the singer, who took to social media on Oct. 10 to accuse the store of treating her as if she couldn't afford a $15,000 mechanical singing bird named Molly. She compared her visit that day to the famous scene from "Pretty Woman," in which Julia Roberts' character is turned away from a pricey store.

The store responded with a series of statements pushing back on Clarkson's claims, saying the yellow wooden bird was not for sale and calling what happened a misunderstanding. Clarkson fired back with another post, calling the shop owner "rude" and a "liar."

See inside the Brooklyn store Kelly Clarkson is feuding with

The feud quickly went viral online. Some sided with the New York-owned shop and argued Clarkson was punching down at a local business. Others defended the singer and shared their experiences of being slighted by salespeople.

Adam Rubin, 43, one of the co-owners of Art of Play, told USA TODAY the store has been overwhelmed since Clarkson blasted the shop to her 8.8 million followers on X. He said the store's phone and emails have been flooded with threatening messages, and their neighbors have been doxxed.

At the same time, sales have surged and they're seeing a spike in foot traffic. In the wake of the controversy, Rubin said the bird is now on sale and upped the price to $15 million.

"This has been a very surreal experience," he said.

Art of Play store owner fears safety of workers after Kelly Clarkson visit

Rubin said the day after Clarkson's post, the store began receiving threatening phone calls and nasty reviews online. He said a neighbor called the police after one person entered the store and accused its employees of racially profiling Clarkson.

"We are afraid for the safety of our shopkeepers," Rubin said. "Kelly Clarkson has put us in danger."

In her initial post, Clarkson said she was "literally was looked at as if I couldn't afford" the bird, "and was told he could find something comparable for me." In Art of Play's social media responses , the company said the bird "is permanently attached to the wall and isn't for sale" but that it offered to show her another singing bird made by a different artist, which cost $2,000.

Art of Play's eccentric collection of home goods and puzzles includes everything from a $1,200 applause machine to custom playing cards. There's a 26-seat theater in the back where magic shows are put on.

Rubin said no one in the shop recognized Clarkson when she walked in. He added that the store was "packed" and that Clarkson was there for "less than five minutes."

"We treated her like a normal person but apparently that did not live up to her expectations," Rubin said, noting Clarkson allegedly scolded an employee. He did not provide further details.

"Nothing happened in this shop to justify her scolding our shopkeeper on the way out, but I could let that go. Everybody has a bad day," he said. "But things changed when she used her platform to attack us. It's asymmetrical social warfare."

Art of Play lists Molly the bird on sale for $15M

Clarkson has pushed back on the shop's claim that Molly the bird was not for sale. In a post on X , Clarkson included a photo of a price tag next to the bird that reads "$15,000."

Rubin said the price tag did not refer to Molly. Instead, the tag showed how much it would cost to order a custom bird from Seattle artist Bliss Kolb.

"We have our automaton. So many people asked about it that we put a price on it," Rubin said. "We talked to the creator and if someone showed serious interest, we would reach out to him about getting them an automaton.

"They take years to make," he added. "This is not something that's sitting in a warehouse."

Kelly Clarkson through the years, from 'American Idol' to superstar

Since Kelly Clarkson earned the title of the first "American Idol" winner in 2002, the pop star's career has flourished, making it impossible for fans to "Breakaway." Look back on her path to stardom, beginning here at the 66th Grammy Awards in Los Angeles on Feb. 4, 2024.

With all the attention, Rubin said he decided to list the bird for sale for $15 million.

articles.title: In 2012, Taylor Swift donated $4 million to Nashville’s country music museum; 14 years later, its education centre gives local artists a platform
articles.summary: Discover how Taylor Swift's generous donation to the Country Music Hall of Fame has transformed an education center into a platform for local artists, including students and individuals with developmental disabilities, showcased in the 'Connection' exhibition.
articles.body: Taylor Swift’s $4 million contribution to Nashville’s Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum helped establish an education centre designed to make music history more interactive. Fourteen years later, the space is highlighting a different kind of talent, with a new exhibition featuring artwork by local school students and artists with developmental disabilities.Titled ‘Connection’, the exhibition opened in April 2026 at the Taylor Swift Education Centre. It features posters created by students from Metro Nashville Public Schools and artists associated with Friends Life Community, a nonprofit that supports adults with developmental disabilities. The project was developed in partnership with Hatch Show Print, the museum’s historic letterpress shop.In its official announcement on April 2, 2026, the Country Music Hall of Fame and Museum explained that participants explored the printing shop’s history and learned how to turn their ideas into posters. The finished pieces reflect themes including empathy, relationships and social causes, using words and images to communicate messages that matter to their creators.How did students and artists create their posters?Students from Cane Ridge High School, Hume-Fogg High School, Stratford High School and Nashville School of the Arts took part in a workshop at Hatch Show Print. They explored the shop’s collection, learned about poster design and experimented with printing shapes made from foam and sponges.The workshop gave them a chance to try a traditional printing technique rather than simply learn about it. Their experiments helped shape the posters displayed in the exhibition, with each participant bringing a personal idea to the project.Artists from Friends Life Community also contributed their work. Grant, Meghan and Sam collaborated with Jennifer Haston, the organisation’s visual arts programme coordinator, and Jim Sherraden, Hatch Show Print’s master printer emeritus.The resulting collection brings together different styles and perspectives. Some posters use lettering and colour to communicate a message, while others rely on imagery to express an idea. Displaying the works side by side gives visitors a glimpse of how differently people can interpret a shared theme.The centre behind the exhibitionSwift’s donation supported the museum’s capital campaign and helped make the education centre possible. The two-storey facility opened in 2013 and offers classrooms, a studio, an interactive gallery and spaces for educational activities.Its programmes introduce students and families to country music through hands-on experiences, including art-making and songwriting. The museum has also used the centre to showcase artwork by young people, giving students opportunities to respond to its collections and collaborate with local artists.‘Connection’ builds on that work by bringing school students and artists associated with Friends Life Community into the same exhibition. It also expands the centre’s focus beyond learning about music, showing how creative activities can help participants develop new skills and share their ideas with the public.A place for local voicesThe exhibition offers a look at what can happen when a cultural institution works with schools and community organisations. Participants were able to learn a traditional craft, make something of their own and see their work displayed in a public setting.For the museum, the project adds another chapter to the education centre’s ongoing programme of workshops and exhibitions. For visitors, it provides an opportunity to discover artwork shaped by the experiences and viewpoints of people from across Nashville.According to the museum’s official exhibition page, ‘Connection’ is scheduled to remain on display until spring 2027, with admission included in museum tickets.Get the latest Bollywood & Entertainment News, and more. articles.title: White House official defends Teresa Giudice’s visit as critics slam reality star’s ex-husband’s pardon push
articles.summary: Lynne Patton shared her cocaine addiction story and the intervention by Eric Trump and Lara Trump that shaped her belief in second chances for Joe Giudice.
articles.body: A senior White House official with longstanding ties to "The Real Housewives of New Jersey" star Teresa Giudice is addressing whether her ex-husband, Joe Giudice, deserves a second chance, while emphasizing that any presidential pardon decision rests solely with President Donald Trump. Lynne Patton, deputy assistant to the president for coalition policy and engagement, took to Instagram to explain why Teresa Giudice and her daughter, Gia Giudice, were invited to the White House for Columbus Day and Italian American heritage celebrations. Patton's comments about Joe, who was deported to Italy after serving time for fraud-related offenses, also addressed the family's efforts to secure a presidential pardon. ‘RHONJ’ ALUM JOE GIUDICE SAYS HE SHOULDN’T HAVE BEEN DEPORTED AFTER FRAUD CONVICTION Patton emphasized that she has no authority over presidential pardons but offered a personal message about redemption and second chances. "For those inquiring @teresagiudice and her daughter, @_giagiudice, were at the White House at the invitation of the President & First Lady in honor of Columbus Day & Italian-American heritage. I have known Teresa and her family, including @joe.giudice, for nearly two decades," Patton began her post. "I’ve attended family gatherings at their former New Jersey homes where Joe taught me how to roll meatballs & Teresa’s beloved father once showed me how to make his famous homemade wine. I am not in charge of pardons. Nor do I decide who receives them." She added, "That is the President’s sole decision based upon recommendations from the White House Pardon Czar, @alicemariefree, and White House Counsel." Patton then shared her own experience with addiction and the second chance she said the Trump family gave her. Patton said she relapsed into cocaine addiction while working at the Trump Organization in 2013, crediting Eric Trump and Lara Trump with staging an intervention that she said saved her life. Her experience, she said, shaped her belief in second chances. "To date, I have been drug-free for 13 years. They could have fired me. But instead, they told me that I was worth saving. Even when I didn’t believe that myself. Instead of sidelining me, they gave me more responsibility. I worked harder. Stayed in the office longer. Arrived earlier. More importantly, I earned back their trust & friendship. In turn, that translated into more self-confidence and earned promotions — including a personal request from their father to join him in D.C. It rebuilt my determination to succeed & help others do the same." Patton also cited her Christian faith and the importance of a father's presence in his children's lives. TODD AND JULIE CHRISLEY HOME FOR HOLIDAYS AFTER TRUMP PARDONS END PRISON TIME "With that said, my faith in God compels me to believe that a father’s place is in the home. Statistics confirm the same. More importantly, so does the Bible. Charlie Kirk often declared that the biblical role of the father to his child is to be their protector, both physically and spiritually. Quality time is everything. And no, it is never too late to be the provider who God intended every father to be," Patton added. "Do I believe that Joe deserves a second chance? Unfortunately, it is not my place to decide. But what I do know is that one of his beautiful daughters desperately needs him now more than ever. And even God supports that." Joe was deported to Italy in 2019 after serving 41 months in federal prison for financial crimes. He has been living in the Bahamas, while his four daughters remain in the United States. Gia has publicly advocated for her father's return to the United States. Joe sought a presidential pardon in June 2025, and Gia said in August 2026 that the family had filed a humanitarian packet as part of its efforts to bring him home. A presidential pardon would not automatically guarantee Joe's return to the United States. According to the Justice Department, a pardon can eliminate certain grounds for deportation, but its immigration consequences depend on the circumstances of the case. The 80-year-old Rocky star is a father to five children

Sylvester Stallone says he's working hard to foot the bill for his daughter Sophia Stallone 's upcoming wedding.

"Oh, man, it's almost embarrassing to say — but I can't retire," Sylvester replied, eliciting laughs from the studio audience. "I can't retire."

Sylvester praised his future son-in-law on Live , calling him "a great guy." He also revealed that Sheehan asked him for his blessing before popping the question to Sophia.

"He actually asked for her hand," the action star said, prompting Ripa, 56, to joke, "He must have been terrified!"

Qué suerte he tenido de tener los padres que me han tocado. PABLO MOTOS. Como a los 10 años tuviste una experiencia con la muerte. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Sí, con 10 años estaba medio dormida con mi madre, y ella estaba hablando con mi tía Aurora sobre alguien a quien habían enterrado, me desperté de un salto gritando que no me quería morir. Me tiré un año llorando porque no me quería morir, no comía ni nada. Me llevaron al médico porque estaban asustados. Se me fue pasando con el tiempo, pero me quedó un pequeño trauma, yo al cementerio no voy nunca, iré una sola vez, cuando me lleven para no volver. PABLO MOTOS. En el libro hablas sobre cuando falleció tu hermano y decidiste no contárselo a tu madre. MARÍA DEL MONTE. Sí, me llamó mi hermano mayor por teléfono, para darme la noticia, y tenía sentada al lado a mi madre, que tenía noventa años. Tuve que disimular para no contárselo y me pasé año y medio engañándola, diciéndole que mi hermano estaba bien cada vez que me preguntaba. Dudaba si estaba haciendo bien o no, en no contárselo. Ese estado de ansiedad prolongada durante tanto tiempo, para mí fue terrorífico. PABLO MOTOS. Tú dices que has visto y sentido a personas fallecidas. MARÍA DEL MONTE. He sentido perfectamente a mi hermano en mi casa, le he olido. Pero no solo yo, mi madre, antes de morir, decía que veía a mi padre y a mi hermano ya fallecidos por casa, ella me decía: "Les veo, pero no como a ti, les veo diferente". PABLO MOTOS. Cuando estuviste la vez anterior, dijiste que España iba a ganar el Mundial y ganó. Ahora te pregunto, ¿quién va a ganar las elecciones? MARÍA DEL MONTE. Las elecciones creo que no las va a ganar ningún partido político, solo le pido a Dios que no perdamos nosotros. Yo no sé de política, pero creo que la primera misión de los políticos es velar por los intereses del país, mirando por los ciudadanos, no por ellos. PABLO MOTOS. Hay quien dice que dijiste públicamente que eras lesbiana una vez que murió tu madre. ¿Te has sentido alguna vez dentro de un armario? MARÍA DEL MONTE. Nunca, y tengo dos argumentos maravillosos: uno, que no quepo, y otro, que no he tenido la necesidad. Yo no he vivido una infancia ni una juventud reprimida, siempre he tenido mucha libertad en mi entorno. Mi madre ha sabido siempre cómo era su hija; ¿cómo no va a conocer una madre a sus hijos?

articles.title: Tupac Shakur murder case: Duane 'Keffe D' Davis gets 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating rapper's death
articles.summary: Duane \"Keffe D\" Davis was sentenced Tuesday to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur who was gunned down off
articles.body: Duane "Keffe D" Davis was sentenced Tuesday to 40 years to life in prison for orchestrating the murder of rap icon Tupac Shakur who was gunned down off the Las Vegas Strip over 30 years ago.Davis, 63, was convicted in August of first-degree murder with the use of a deadly weapon. He is the only person ever charged in the death of Shakur, whose popularity was peaking at age 25.Prosecutor Marc DiGiacomo said Tuesday that whatever sentence the court imposes, Davis is "guaranteed to die" behind bars."It's not just about losing a family member," DiGiacomo said as Shakur's sister Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur nods her head in the audience.The killing went unsolved for years until Davis, a former leader of the South Side Compton Crips, gave interviews and published his role in the shooting in his 2019 tell-all memoir.DiGiacomo said Davis was trying to profit off a killing that he committed, and for that he does not deserve the minimum sentence."In my mind he deserves the maximum possible sentence," DiGiacomo said.Davis spoke briefly in court, telling Judge Carli Kierny he wants items back that police took from his house, including his pictures. Asked if there was anything else he wanted to say, Davis said: "No I'm good."Davis' lawyer, Michael Sanft said he plans to appeal the verdict. Sanft said prosecutors waited too long to bring the case.On the night of Sept. 7, 1996, Shakur was in the passenger seat of a black BMW with music mogul Marion "Suge" Knight when a white Cadillac pulled up at a red light, and shots erupted. Shakur was shot multiple times and died six days later, while Knight survived.Shakur is considered one of the most influential and versatile rappers of all time and had a burgeoning film career as an actor at the time of his death. His legend has only grown since. His songs still resonate among fans with themes of hardship, love and Black struggles.In his memoir, Davis explained how Shakur and his entourage beat up Davis' nephew hours before the shooting in Las Vegas. He said he sought retaliation, and that he was in the passenger seat of the Cadillac and passed the gun to the backseat, where shots were fired. Davis had spoken to detectives years before but avoided prosecution because of an agreement he made with law enforcement.During the weekslong trial, prosecutors relied on Davis' own statements he made to law enforcement and documentarians. They argued Davis orchestrated the shooting and provided the gun used in Shakur's death, which was the result of a rivalry between the South Side Compton Crips and Mob Piru. Davis' defense attorney pointed to a lack of physical evidence that connected his client to the 30-year-old crime, and he portrayed Davis as a liar who was trying to make money.After nine days of hearing testimony in August, the jury deliberated for three hours before turning over the guilty verdict.Shakur was an icon, a brotherShakur's family spoke at the sentencing, including his siblings Maurice "Mopreme" Shakur and Sekyiwa "Set" Shakur.Following the verdict, prosecutor Binu Palal said that to many people, Shakur was an icon or an idea, "but to the family, Tupac Shakur was a brother, a son, a cousin, a loved person ripped from them 30 years ago."Palal said the family had to sit through years of Davis "bragging about killing someone they loved.""They loved that man. And the arrogance that Mr. Davis had in expressing his joy in killing that man ultimately was his undoing," Palal said.Prosecutors say they have insufficient evidence to charge anyone elseDavis is the only person to be charged and convicted in the killing of Shakur. The three other people who allegedly were in the Cadillac - including Davis' nephew Orlando "Baby Lane" Anderson who Davis said was the one who pulled the trigger - have died.Sean "Diddy" Combs and his alleged role were brought up often throughout the trial. Witnesses testified Combs used members of the South Side Compton Crips for security for Bad Boy Records. In his book and public statements, Davis alleged Combs offered him money to kill Shakur and Knight. Combs, who is serving a four-year prison sentence after being convicted of prostitution-related offenses, has repeatedly denied any involvement in the death of Shakur.Clark County District Attorney Steve Wolfson has said his office doesn't believe it has sufficient evidence to charge anyone else."But like any other case, if we come into more information, more evidence, we can always consider filing additional charges," he said following the guilty verdict. articles.title: Actress Amanda Seyfried rejected TV role over nonstop sex scenes, refused to get 'naked with a stranger'
articles.summary: Amanda Seyfried says she's no longer willing to be naked with strangers on set, joining Hollywood actresses pushing back against intimate scene demands.
articles.body: Actress Amanda Seyfried revealed during a Sunday conversation with Alec Baldwin at the Hamptons International Film Festival in East Hampton, New York, that she rejected a television series because of its frequent sex scenes, explaining that she has become increasingly uncomfortable performing intimate scenes as she gets older. "I passed on a show where I would have to have sex all the time because of the sex. Doesn't matter [who it's with]… I don't want to do it. I'm uncomfortable with it. I'm not into it right now," Seyfried said, according to People Magazine. Seyfried's decision echoes concerns raised by other Hollywood actresses, including Gina Gershon, who told Fox News Digital in March that she rejected a starring role in the 1981 horror film "Friday the 13th Part 2" after learning her character would appear topless. "I was offered a lead in that movie," Gershon said, adding that the nudity "definitely felt kind of exploitative to me." 'GAME OF THRONES' STAR LENA HEADEY SAYS OUTRAGE OVER INFAMOUS NUDE SCENE LEFT HER STUNNED Seyfried, 40, said her feelings about portraying romantic relationships on screen have changed significantly since the beginning of her career, when she was more enthusiastic about filming intimate scenes. "Maybe if [the project] came along again [at a later point], maybe I'd be in a different space. But I don't want to deal with being naked with a stranger," Seyfried said. The Oscar-nominated actress previously acknowledged feeling pressured to participate in uncomfortable scenes when she was younger. In a 2022 interview with Porter magazine, Seyfried described participating in scenes without underwear at 19 because she feared upsetting people and jeopardizing her career. "Oh, I know why: I was 19, and I didn't want to upset anybody and I wanted to keep my job. That's why," Seyfried said. SYDNEY SWEENEY DEFENDS 'EUPHORIA' NUDITY AND REVEALS A POLE DANCING SCENE WAS CUT FROM SEASON THREE Other actresses have described similar experiences. In 2023, Christina Ricci revealed on "The View" that she was once threatened with legal action after refusing to perform an intimate scene in a particular way. "Someone threatened to sue me once because I didn't want to do this sex scene in a certain way," Ricci said. Keira Knightley previously revealed that becoming a mother changed her willingness to appear nude on camera. The actress incorporated a no-nudity clause into her contracts, allowing her greater control over intimate scenes. CATE BLANCHETT MOURNS HOW #METOO GOT 'KILLED VERY QUICKLY,' STILL 'SYSTEMIC LAYER OF ABUSE' Not every actress has taken the same approach. In June, Fox News Digital reported that "Euphoria" star Sydney Sweeney rejected creator Sam Levinson's suggestion to reduce nudity in the show's third season, believing the scenes were relevant to her character's storyline. Hollywood has introduced additional protections for actors filming intimate scenes. Jessica Steinrock, an intimacy coordinator, told Fox News Digital that coordinators help establish expectations and consent during production. "[Intimacy Coordinator] is a relatively new role. It really hit its stride kind of in 2018 when HBO made their commitment to having an intimacy coordinator on all their film sets," she said. "An intimacy coordinator is there to provide safety and framework for scenes of intimacy. Those are scenes of simulated sex, simulated genital contact, or scenes of nudity." CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE Under SAG-AFTRA's guidelines, performers must receive advance notice of expected nudity or simulated sex acts, and producers generally must provide written nudity riders at least 48 hours before filming. The union also established a collective bargaining agreement covering intimacy coordinators in 2025. Seyfried, who shares two children with actor Thomas Sadoski, said motherhood has further influenced her willingness to establish boundaries, both professionally and personally. articles.title: Judi Dench blasts 'trigger warnings' ruining stories: 'Drives me wild'
articles.summary: Actress Judi Dench called trigger warnings in theater and movies "mollycoddling" in her upcoming memoir, arguing audiences should expect to be provoked.
articles.body: Dame Judi Dench decried trigger warnings in theaters and movies as "mollycoddling," telling U.K. outlet The Times Friday that it "drives [her] wild" to see them. The 91-year-old English actress expressed the thoughts in an excerpt for Dench's upcoming memoir, "Is It Too Late to Make a Run for It?" As a stage and screen veteran, Dench claimed that placing trigger warnings in front of productions has gone beyond age limits or sound effects. "I think they have gone too far," Dench said. "It's mollycoddling. If you're that sensitive, don't go to the theater. UNIVERSITY THAT PUT OVER 200 TRIGGER WARNINGS ON SHAKESPEARE WRITINGS SAYS REQUEST CAME FROM STUDENTS "By all means, keep the warnings about strobe lighting and gunshots, and obviously there should be age limits for children, but that's about it. Otherwise, where will it end?" Dench also joked that trigger warnings have potentially ruined classic stories by removing surprises and watering down provocative content. "The trigger warnings before 'Titus Andronicus' would be longer than the play. And if you overdo the warnings, doesn’t it take away from the audience’s enjoyment of the story? Do you tell them that the butler did it in an Agatha Christie play so as not to shock them? "Besides, in the safety of a theater or cinema, I want to be triggered, excited, stimulated, provoked and disturbed, to be taken out of my comfort zone. Isn’t that what makes theater and films so thrilling?" Dench said. ‘HOUSE OF THE DRAGON’ STAR MATT SMITH SLAMS TRIGGER WARNINGS ON TV SHOWS: ‘ISN’T BEING SHOCKED THE POINT?’ "And who knows what might trigger people? Balloons, clowns, buttons. ... I have a friend who doesn’t like bananas. She feels physically sick every time she sees one. Should supermarkets put up warning signs in the fruit and veg aisle? It drives me wild." Fox News Digital reached out to Dench's representative for comment. The English actress made similar comments about content advisories in a 2024 interview in which she expressed sympathy for some arguments but ultimately suggested those too sensitive should simply not go to the theater. "I can see why they exist, and it is preparing people, I suppose. But if you’re that sensitive, don’t go to the theater because you could be very shocked," Dench said. BILL MAHER RAILS AGAINST TRIGGER WARNINGS IN COLLEGES, ENTERTAINMENT: 'HOW WEAK MY COUNTRY HAS BECOME' In a comment to Fox News Digital, film critic and "Hollywood in Toto" podcast host Christian Toto called it a "sad state of affairs" that Dench's comments would be considered surprising but celebrated them regardless. "Dench's statement on trigger warnings is obvious, but it still needs to be said today. It's especially helpful coming from an artist. Almost anything in art can be triggering, all depending on the audience. If your beloved dog died last week, any story with a sick pup can be 'triggering.' Art is meant to challenge us, to question our beliefs and offer new perspectives on older ideas. All of the above might be triggering today," Toto said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "So deal with it, or don't consume art. This kind of wisdom is rare in Hollywood. Kudos for Dench for lighting the way to sanity."

articles.title: Jeremy Strong Texted Jessica Chastain After ‘Other Mommy’ Obliterated ‘Social Reckoning’ at the Box Office
articles.summary: Jeremy Strong and Jessica Chastain are having some fun over their new films competing against each other at the box office.
articles.body:
Jeremy Strong and Jessica Chastain are having some fun over their new films competing against each other at the box office.

Last week, Strong and Chastain both had new movies release – " The Social Reckoning " and " Other Mommy " – and the two clashed at the box office . "Other Mommy" opened to $27.5 million while "The Social Reckoning" arrived DOA with only $5.5 million. Strong, who plays Mark Zuckerberg in the Aaron Sorkin film, sent a text to Chastain with a Vulture article proclaiming "'Other Mommy' Spanks 'The Social Reckoning' At The Box Office."

"Omg," Chastain responded in the texts that she later shared on her Instagram story.

Strong responded to that with two emojis: the middle finger and a face blowing a kiss.

"These pics are hysterical," Chastain responded. The pics in question show Chastain – as either the regular or Demonic Mommy – staring at the camera while Strong as Zuckerberg looks down at the ground.

Made on a $19 million budget, "Other Mommy" stars Chastain as a mom who discovers that there is a vicious doppelganger of herself that is haunting her daughter. The film should be able to clear its low break-even point theatrically as it has also grossed $17.6 million overseas from 50 markets for a $45 million global start.

"The Social Reckoning" earned its abysmal opening numbers and landed at at No. 5 on the box office charts just ahead of the third weekend of Universal/DreamWorks' animated flop "Forgotten Island" with $4.5 million. By comparison, Sorkin's previous film about the Facebook creator, "The Social Network," opened to $22.6 million in the fall of 2010.

articles.title: Billy Crystal says he no longer trusts God after losing home of 46 years then his longtime friend Rob Reiner
articles.summary: Billy Crystal says he no longer trusts God after losing his Pacific Palisades home in the wildfires and the death of close friend Rob Reiner.
articles.body: Billy Crystal is opening up about how a devastating year changed his relationship with God. During an interview with CBS Sunday Morning, the comedian, 78, opened up about how losing his longtime Pacific Palisades home in the January 2025 wildfires and the death of his close friend Rob Reiner greatly impacted his faith. Crystal was asked whether he had been speaking with God after the painful losses. The actor referenced his previous one-man show, "700 Sundays," in which he described conversations with God, before offering a stark response. BILLY CRYSTAL DESCRIBES PAIN OF LOSING HOME IN PALISADES FIRE AT FIREAID BENEFIT CONCERT: ‘FELL TO MY KNEES’ "No, ’cause I don’t trust Him," Crystal said. "Too many bad things have happened," he added. "The Earth is in bad shape. This is a weird, scary time. So no, not anymore." Crystal’s longtime home was destroyed in the Palisades fire after he and his wife, Janice, lived there for 46 years. The couple raised their children and grandchildren in the house, which Crystal described as a "magical place." Speaking at a benefit weeks after the disaster, Crystal recalled visiting the remains of what was once his home. ERIKA KIRK PENS ESSAY ON GRIEF AS READERS GAIN INSIGHTS INTO WRENCHING PAST YEAR "When we were finally able to get back to our house in the Palisades, which I lived in for 46 years, like thousands of you, our house now looked like this," Crystal said, before a photo of the aftermath of the Palisades Fire appeared on the screen. "I stepped onto the grounds and fell to my knees and I wailed. I had not cried like that since I was 15 years old, and I was told that my father had just died. I remember looking in the mirror back then with my whole life ahead of me thinking, ‘What’s my life gonna be like without him?'" "And now folks, I'm 76-years-old, without a mirror and a lot less life to ponder thinking, ‘What is my life going to be like without our home?’" Crystal asked. The loss became the inspiration for Crystal’s new Broadway show, "860," which is named after the street address of the home. The production recreates his home office onstage and explores his family, career, memories and grief. NICK REINER INDICTED IN MURDERS OF PARENTS ROB REINER, MICHELE SINGER REINER AT BRENTWOOD HOME "860" also reflects on the loss of Reiner, who was killed with his wife, Michele, in December 2025. Crystal said he and Reiner had been together at a holiday party the night before their deaths. "We said goodbye," Crystal recalled. "And then … what?!?" Despite the tragedies, Crystal said humor has helped him move forward. "That’s what I do," he said when asked how he finds humor during the darkest moments. "It’s a healer." Crystal said performing "860" has already helped him process the loss of his home and friends. articles.title: Incredible winning images from Wildlife Photographer of the Year 2026
articles.summary: A heartbreaking image of an elephant carrying a dead calf has been named the overall winner of the 2026 Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition.
articles.body: A heartbreaking image of an elephant carrying a dead calf has been named the overall winner of the 2026 Wildlife Photographer of the Year competition. The image, named “The Aftermath,” was taken by Italian photographer Federico Veronesi. It shows a female elephant carrying the calf in Namibia, according to a statement from the Natural History Museum, which organizes the competition, on Tuesday. “This photograph works on so many levels. Emotionally it’s a gut punch, heartbreakingly poignant. Intellectually it’s proof that animals have cognition,” said Kathy Moran, chair of the competition’s jury, in the statement. Meanwhile, Oscar Whitfield won the Young Wildlife Photographer of the Year award for his photo of a dung beetle pushing its prize. Named “Labour of Love,” Whitfield captured the image by lying flat on the ground as the beetle moved past his lens. “This is exceptionally well done. Photographing such a small, constantly moving subject is challenging, yet the image feels so intentional,” said jury member Jasper Doest in the statement. “The composition reveals an entire story and by doing so the photograph quietly reveals how life cycles depend on what we often overlook or dismiss,” Doest added. The jury also selected winners in more than a dozen other categories, all of which will form part of an exhibition that opens on October 16 at the Natural History Museum in London, England. The competition received a record-breaking 65,403 entries from 121 countries and territories around the world, organizers said. “This year’s winning photographs demonstrate the extraordinary power of wildlife photography to help us see nature differently,” said Doug Gurr, director of the museum, in the statement. “Together they remind us that every species plays a role in the complex web of life, and why understanding and protecting the natural world has never been more important.”

articles.body: Joe Manganiello is opening up about the secret health battle that nearly "took his life" over seven years. Manganiello sat down with "CBS Mornings" to discuss his health and his newly released memoir, "Bloodlines." During his appearance, the actor told Gayle King he was offered the role as the main villain, Deathstroke, in Ben Affleck's canceled "Batman" movie. My entire large intestine had turned to pus, and it was about to explode," he continued. "They took it out, and the surgery left me with an ostomy bag. articles.title: UFS: inscrições abertas para Música, Letras Libras e Veterinária | G1
articles.standfirst: Editais englobam os vestibulares 2027 de Música e Letras Libras, além da matrícula para o curso de Medicina Veterinária pelo Pronera.
articles.summary: A UFS abriu inscrições para os vestibulares de Música e Letras Libras 2027 e convocou aprovados em Medicina Veterinária pelo Pronera para matrícula.
articles.body:
Universidade Federal de Sergipe — Foto: Jackson Bandeira/UFS/Divulgação

A Universidade Federal de Sergipe (UFS) publicou três novos editais relativos a processos seletivos e matrículas para cursos de graduação. As seleções contemplam os vestibulares de 2027 para Licenciatura em Música e Licenciatura em Letras Libras, além da convocação para matrícula institucional para Medicina Veterinária, vinculada ao Programa Nacional de Educação na Reforma Agrária (PRONERA), para o semestre 2026.1.

De acordo com a UFS, o processo seletivo para o curso de Música, na modalidade Licenciatura, oferta 50 vagas para o turno noturno, no campus de São Cristóvão. Podem se inscrever candidatos que já concluíram ou estão concluindo o ensino médio e que tenham prestado o Exame Nacional do Ensino Médio (Enem) entre os anos de 2022 e 2026. O processo seletivo ocorrerá em duas etapas: avaliação de conhecimentos específicos (teórica e prática), de caráter eliminatório, e de classificação utilizando a nota do Enem. As provas teóricas estão marcadas para o dia 6 de dezembro, enquanto as práticas acontecerão entre 7 e 9 de dezembro. As inscrições devem ser feitas de 20 a 27 de outubro, pelo site da Prograd, com taxa de R$ 60,00. Candidatos que atendam aos requisitos de baixa renda e estejam inscritos no CadÚnico podem solicitar isenção da taxa entre os dias 13 e 15 de outubro. Mais detalhes podem ser consultados no edital .

Para o curso de Letras Libras (Licenciatura), que funciona no turno matutino em São Cristóvão, são ofertadas 30 vagas. O curso tem natureza bilíngue, sendo 22 vagas do Grupo A prioritariamente destinadas a pessoas surdas ou com deficiência auditiva, e 8 vagas do Grupo B abertas a ouvintes. O cronograma de inscrições acompanha o Vestibular de Música, ocorrendo de 20 a 27 de outubro no site da Prograd, também com taxa de R$ 60,00 e período de isenção entre 13 e 15 de outubro. Os candidatos do Grupo A contarão com provas em Libras e apoio de tradutores e intérpretes no dia da aplicação. Para conferir a distribuição completa de vagas, acesse o edital.

Matrícula Pronera - Medicina Veterinária 2026.1

Candidatos aprovados no processo seletivo especial para o curso de Medicina Veterinária, em regime de alternância (Pronera), devem ficar atentos ao prazo de matrícula institucional, que se inicia no dia 14 de outubro e se encerra no dia 19 de outubro de 2026. O envio de toda a documentação (em formato PDF) deve ser feito exclusivamente pelo Portal de Ingresso da UFS (via SIGAA). O edital detalha os procedimentos de validação documental exigidos, incluindo a aferição fenotípica para candidatos autodeclarados pretos ou pardos (cujo resultado fotodocumental será divulgado em 20 de outubro) e a análise da Junta Médica e Serviço Social para cotistas. Para acessar os anexos documentais e o cronograma completo, confira o edital.

♬ Sobrinho de Lô Borges (1952 – 2025) e de Márcio Borges, irmãos que compuseram parte do cancioneiro essencial do Clube da Esquina, Rodrigo Borges reforça os vínculos familiares no terceiro álbum, “Transverso”.

Programado para 13 de novembro, o álbum “Transverso” tem repertório calcado na música de Minas Gerais, estado natal do cantor, compositor e violonista revelado há 15 anos com a edição do álbum “Qualquer palavra” em 2011.

Nesse álbum inicial, Rodrigo gravou “Outro cais” (Marilton Borges e Duca Leal, 1980), música que reaparece em “Transverso” em gravação feita com o toque do piano Fender Rhodes de Marilton Borges, pai de Rodrigo e um dos compositores da canção (também revivida por Maria Rita no corrente show “Redescobrir vol. 2” ).

Ao longo das oito faixas do álbum “Transverso”, Rodrigo Borges apresenta três composições autorais – “Eu sigo a lua”, “Quando o sol renascer” e “Um amor” – entre regravações de “Onde a gente está” (Lô Borges e Márcio Borges, 2010) e “Sonho real” (Lô Borges e Ronaldo Bastos, 1984).

Gravada por Rodrigo em dueto com a cantora mineira Roberta Campos, “Sonho real” é a música escolhida para anunciar o álbum “Transverso” em single agendado para 30 de outubro.

Rodrigo Borges (voz, vocais e violões de aço) gravou o álbum “Transverso” com os toques dos músicos Beto Lopes (baixo, trompete e guitarras), Christiano Caldas (pianos, teclados e sintetizadores), Diogo Gomes (trompete), Jorge Continentino (saxofone e flauta), Lincoln Cheib (percussão e bateria) e Marlon Sette (trombone).

articles.title: Adriana Calcanhotto e Arnaldo Antunes sobre parceria: 'O impulso de ir ao dicionário é o mesmo' | G1
articles.standfirst: Em entrevista ao g1, dupla fala sobre o processo de composição do novo disco, a influência das redes sociais nas letras e como um show em festival virou projeto de carreira.
articles.summary: Em entrevista ao g1, dupla fala sobre o processo de composição do novo disco, a influência das redes sociais nas letras e como um show em festival virou projeto de carreira.
articles.body:
Amigos há décadas, Adriana Calcanhotto e Arnaldo Antunes já trocavam algumas composições, já dividiram o palco... mas, até hoje, nunca tinham gravado um projeto juntos. Quando finalmente fizeram, foi pra valer: os dois cantores, compositores e poetas se uniram para o disco "Vice-Versa", lançado no dia 22 de setembro, e se preparam para uma turnê conjunta.

A parceria, mais que natural, é fruto de um show conjunto que eles fizeram no Coala Festival, em 2024. Vez em quando, esses shows no modelo "Fulano convida Ciclano", típicos de festivais, rendem encontros especiais: dele nasceu um álbum de inéditas (tem só uma regravação: "Sorriso Livro", do Timbalada).

"Vice-Versa" vai do samba ao rock, com versos diretos com a assinatura moderna e fina de ambos. E atestou tanto a parceria dos dois que, na verdade, quase todas as músicas são cantadas em uníssono.

"É uma confirmação estética de que não é um disco de um ou de outro. Você ouve cada um dos dois, mas o barato é ouvir essa terceira voz", disse Adriana ao g1 .

Ao g1, Adriana e Arnaldo relembraram a criação de "Vice-Versa", a influência das redes sociais nas letras e como um show em festival virou projeto de carreira. Veja abaixo:

Arnaldo Antunes e Adriana Calcanhotto anunciam trabalho e turnê conjuntos — Foto: Divulgação/Leo Aversa

g1: Quando eu vi que vocês lançaram um disco juntos, pensei: "Nossa, eu queria ser uma mosquinha lá no estúdio para acompanhar esse processo". Então eu queria saber como era um dia de composições e gravações, quem chegava com o quê, como foi esse processo.

Adriana Calcanhotto : Olha, o processo começou assim: eu resolvi fazer uma melodia para o projeto, pensando no Arnaldo, que não fosse nada que eu já tinha antes, nenhum trecho de nada, não peguei pedaço de coisa nenhuma.

Sentei no violão, fiz uma melodia e mandei para ele: "Vamos começar daqui". Aí fui para a casa dele, em São Paulo, cheguei lá e ele tinha duas letras para essa melodia. Começou assim.

Arnaldo Antunes : Eu fiquei na dúvida, acabei fazendo duas letras diferentes para ela escolher.

Adriana: Que era o "Agora Juntos". E o "Agora Juntos" era um tratado, o nosso. Eu achei incrível, muito bem colocada a melodia, mas sobretudo o que estava falando da gente, do projeto.

Arnaldo: A outra letra que acabou sendo escolhida, claro, foi o "Agora Juntos", feita pensando na gente cantando isso junto no palco. E a outra letra, ela fez outra melodia e, no dia seguinte, já trouxe. Aí a gente começou a fazer junto. Claro que ela trazia alguma melodia que já tinha, eu trazia alguma melodia que já tinha, a gente fazia a letra junto.

Às vezes partia de uma letra, às vezes de uma melodia, às vezes de um começo de letra com melodia e puxava outras partes. Teve todo tipo de trajeto, mas passamos a fazer junto desde então. A única que eu fiz a letra separado em cima da melodia que ela tinha mandado foi o "Agora Juntos".

g1: Eu vi numa entrevista, acho que da época do Coala, que você, Adriana, falou que era muito tímida para compor com outras pessoas presencialmente. Como foi para você esse processo, tendo tanta admiração pelo Arnaldo e estando ali colaborando juntos?

Adriana: Foi muito interessante porque ele tem muito mais experiência, muito mais parceiros, fez muito mais músicas, vem de uma banda com muita gente, tem o lance com os Tribalistas. Tudo isso num movimento muito diferente do meu. Mas, como a gente se conhece, tem intimidade, e eu sou muito fã do que ele faz, eu me sentia à vontade para propor as coisas.

E vi coisas muito comuns entre a gente: o momento em que não estávamos satisfeitos com uma palavra, o impulso de ir ao dicionário era o mesmo, na mesma hora. Essas coisas me surpreenderam, o que era comum entre a gente. É uma confirmação do modo de trabalhar.

Arnaldo: A busca e a adequação da palavra na melodia, de ter a prosódia certa, de ouvir o que a melodia já está sugerindo. A gente tinha uma busca muito comum no dia a dia do que queria atingir.

Adriana: Eu senti, nos momentos na casa dele, que, quando íamos tomar um café ou olhar o telefone, havia um incômodo mútuo se nenhum dos dois estivesse contente com uma palavra ou com o processo.

Arnaldo: A canção tem que soar natural, não dá para forçar a barra. Essa naturalidade era uma preocupação nossa. Às vezes o caminho que cada um fazia para chegar nisso era um pouco diferente, e isso dava uma surpresa boa quando a coisa encaixava devidamente. Foi muito bom.

g1: Vocês cantam em uníssono boa parte das músicas. E as fotos, o nome, tudo isso brinca com vocês serem dois lados de uma coisa só. Como foi essa decisão? Veio de vocês perceberem que pensavam muito parecido?

Arnaldo: A decisão de cantar juntos a gente nem tomou, fomos cantando e era assim que era. Achamos mais natural cantar junto porque a junção das vozes gerou um perfil vocal novo que mantém a integridade de ambas ao mesmo tempo.

Se você presta atenção na minha voz ou na da Adriana, você ouve cada uma, mas o conjunto forma uma terceira voz. Acho isso muito interessante, deu coesão ao disco todo.

Adriana: É uma confirmação estética de que não é um disco de um ou de outro. A nossa voz é gigante em termos de tessitura. O grave do Arnaldo cantado em oitavas, muito naturalmente... Você ouve cada um dos dois, mas o barato é ouvir essa terceira voz.

Adriana Calcanhotto e Arnaldo Antunes transitam entre samba, balada e indie-rock ao longo do álbum 'Vice-versa' — Foto: Leo Aversa / Divulgação

g1: Uma música que me chamou a atenção de cara foi "As Bancas de Jornais", que é a mais política, tem um comentário... sutil, talvez, mas tem. Queria saber a história dela e o que inspirou vocês a usarem a banca de jornal para falar de algo atual.

Arnaldo: Nem é sutil, é explícita. Pega um ícone, a banca de jornal, que perdeu a sua função original para se tornar outra coisa, para falar desses tempos de consumo absurdo. A visão crítica está desde falar de ultraprocessados para a larica até em falar em bomba nuclear. Você começa falando de excesso de consumo, como a vitrine do capitalismo e do consumo desnecessário e artificial — tudo é diet, light, capinhas.

E, ao mesmo tempo, a convivência da fofura com a violência, a crueldade e a naturalização dos absurdos das guerras.

É mais ou menos como convivemos nos meios digitais: você vê um bicho de pelúcia fofinho e um soco inglês. Essa naturalização da barra pesada convivendo com a fofura.

Adriana: Tem a questão de não haver mais os jornais — a parte ruim das fontes e da verdade, das pós-verdades. Mas é interessante: não tem mais os jornais, mas tem as bancas. O que as bancas viraram? O que elas são agora?

g1: Vocês dois estão na casa dos 60, né? E nesse disco, tem "Na Minha Carne Viva" e outras músicas meio tipo "Cara, eu tô bem resolvido aqui, não vem me dar pitaco não". Eu queria saber o que inspirou, principalmente essa música: se vocês se encontram também nesse lugar de estarem bem-resolvidos, sem precisar mais provar nada para ninguém, mas lidando com o mundo em constante mudança...

Arnaldo: Eu acho essa música tão adolescente [risos]. Não acho que seja uma música pensada para pós-60 anos. Esse pensamento — "eu quero saber da minha vida, não quero conselho" — é muito jovial, acho engraçado. Não sei se é uma música de amadurecimento.

Adriana: Mas tem um componente das redes sociais, onde todo mundo julga muito, toma conta da vida dos outros e acha que sabe o que é melhor para eles. É uma versão dos nossos tempos daquele ditado: "Vai cuidar da sua vida; quem cuida da vida alheia da sua não pode cuidar". Ficar cheio de assunto sobre a vida dos outros significa que a sua está menos interessante.

g1: E essa tem a participação da Marisa Monte nas composições...

Adriana: A Marisa... Nós temos todo esse tempo de relação, amizade e trajetória, eu gravando coisas dele, nos encontrando em shows, mas não tínhamos uma canção até então. Essa canção só existiu por causa de um evento que ela fez. Ela é madrinha dessa nossa parceria. Então, para mim é muito natural a presença dela na nossa roda.

Adriana: O Arnaldo veio para a minha casa no Rio, e combinamos de fazer uma canção para o disco.

Arnaldo: Mas o costume não garante nada, sempre tem o risco de dar certo ou não, e tem esse sabor de aventura a cada encontro.

Adriana: O legal do "Vice-Versa" é que fizemos algumas canções que não entraram. Tiramos a nata daquilo que produzimos, não só em termos de qualidade, mas no recorte do disco, conforme a cara dele ia se definindo. Gosto de termos feito as canções sem sobras forçadas.

g1: E essas escolhas incluem uma regravação (“Sorriso Livro”, do Timbalada). Esse disco tem o Tribalistas "quebrado", já que tem Marisa e Carlinhos entre os compositores.

g1: Por que a escolha dessa regravação do Timbalada?

Adriana: Na primeira reunião na casa do Arnaldo, no primeiro jantar, falamos de várias coisas. Além das canções que poderíamos fazer juntos ou com parceiros, como a Marisa, falamos de músicas que não são do repertório de nenhum de nós, mas que adoraríamos cantar. Ele falou de "Sorriso Livro" como uma canção que adorava.

E eu disse: "Caramba, eu era apaixonada por essa música, ouvia em looping quando lançou". Pronto, foi a primeira certeza: "Sorriso Livro".

Arnaldo: Foi uma sincronicidade. É uma música que eu pensava em gravar há muito tempo e não tinha acontecido. Esperou chegar essa sincronicidade de encontrar a Adriana com o mesmo gosto e paixão por ela. Pensamos em outras que poderiam ser gravadas por nós, mas acabamos querendo mostrar as nossas músicas mesmo. Essa foi a única de fora que permaneceu convictamente.

g1: Essa parceria tem muito a ver com aquele show no Coala em 2024. Esses encontros de duplas em festivais nem sempre dão certo. Como vocês enxergam esse tipo de convite e show?

Arnaldo: No nosso caso deu muito certo; esse disco e essa nova turnê só aconteceram por causa do Coala. Foi tão bom que quisemos mais. Eu entendo que em outros casos pode não dar certo, há uma química imprevisível. Nós topamos porque sabíamos que daria certo, pois já havia afinidade, histórico de participações nos shows um do outro e referências comuns. Deu muito certo e nos motivou a dar prosseguimento ao trabalho conjunto.

Adriana: Eu sabia que com ele não correria o risco de fazer um show burocrático — de cada um cantar seus dois sucessos e pronto. Nós ensaiamos muito, trabalhamos cada detalhe. Se fosse algo casual, eu não teria tanto interesse.

Musicalmente, a química nem sempre acontece entre convidados, mas encontros pontiagudos podem produzir coisas lindas.

g1: Adriana, você gravou "Sonífera Ilha" logo no seu primeiro disco. O que te atraía nessa música e nos Titãs? Parece que a trajetória de vocês já estava entrelaçada.

Adriana: Eu acompanhava a banda e o Arnaldo antes de vir para o Rio e lançar meu disco em 1990. "Sonífera Ilha" era uma música que eu tocava nos shows de voz e violão, pegando aquela faixa melodiosa e fazendo num jeito quase bossa nova. Na gravação do disco ficou um pouco diferente, mas já estava ali. Antes disso, em Porto Alegre, eu já cantava "Comida" e "Não Me Acabo" nos meus shows como intérprete.

g1: Para fechar, vocês devem estar pensando no repertório um do outro. Tem alguma música um do outro (incluindo as que a Adriana regravou) que vocês gostariam de ter gravado ou escrito?

Arnaldo: Tem várias: "Pela Janela", "Quem É Ela"... Várias que eu gostaria de ter cantado. Agora vamos ter a oportunidade de cantar algumas delas.

articles.title: Suspeitos de furtar joalheria na Rua Oscar Freire confessam crime e são liberados; 90% das joias são recuperadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Um dos investigados é um pedreiro contratado pela quadrilha para abrir buracos em imóveis vizinhos e invadir a joalheria. O outro é apontado como receptador.
articles.summary: Um dos investigados é um pedreiro contratado pela quadrilha para abrir buracos em imóveis vizinhos e invadir a joalheria. O outro é apontado como receptador.
articles.body:
Os dois suspeitos detidos por participação no furto a uma joalheria na Rua Oscar Freire, nos Jardins, na Zona Oeste de São Paulo , confessaram o crime à polícia e foram liberados na noite de terça-feira (13), por não terem sido presos em flagrante. Eles foram indiciados por furto qualificado.

Com um dos suspeitos, os policiais encontraram uma bolsa com centenas de peças de prata. O dono da joalheria informou que mais de 90% das joias furtadas foram recuperadas.

Um dos suspeitos é um pedreiro contratado pela quadrilha para abrir buracos em imóveis vizinhos e invadir a joalheria. Identificado por imagens de câmeras de segurança, ele recebeu R$ 300 pelo serviço, de acordo com o delegado Felipe Lopes Pereira, da 2ª Delegacia do Patrimônio do Departamento Estadual de Investigações Criminais (Deic).

Polícia detém dois suspeitos e recupera parte das joias furtadas em invasão a joalheria na Oscar Freire — Foto: Divulgação

O segundo suspeito é apontado como receptador das joias. Ele foi localizado em uma tabacaria no Centro de São Paulo, onde as peças foram encontradas. À polícia, ele admitiu que não participou diretamente do furto, mas sabia que os objetos eram provenientes do crime.

"São mais de cinco indivíduos entre homens e mulheres. Nós ainda estamos trabalhando e num futuro próximo vamos capturar o restante", afirmou o delegado.

O furto ocorreu entre domingo (11) e a madrugada de segunda-feira (12). Os criminosos chegaram ao local por volta das 7h de domingo e deixaram o imóvel à 1h30 da madrugada de segunda-feira, após atravessarem paredes de estabelecimentos vizinhos para chegar à joalheria.

O grupo entrou inicialmente em uma loja em obras na Rua Melo Alves e abriu buracos nas paredes para atravessar duas lojas de roupas até alcançar a joalheria, na Rua Oscar Freire.

Além das joias, avaliadas em aproximadamente R$ 5 milhões, os criminosos levaram mercadorias das lojas de roupas.

Criminosos invadem lojas de roupas para furtar joalheria na Rua Oscar Freire, em SP — Foto: Abraão Cruz/g1

Para dificultar a identificação, eles cobriram câmeras de segurança com papel-alumínio e desativaram os sistemas de alarme. Segundo o depoimento de um dos lojistas à polícia, os suspeitos chegaram a consumir uma garrafa de espumante encontrada no estoque de um dos estabelecimentos invadidos.

O furto foi descoberto quando o gerente da joalheria chegou ao estabelecimento e encontrou a loja revirada. O caso é investigado pela Polícia Civil.

Criminosos invadem duas lojas de roupas para furtar joalheria na Rua Oscar Freire, em SP — Foto: Abraão Cruz/g1

Suspeitos entraram por um imóvel ao lado que está em obras, bloquearam câmeras com papel alumínio e desativaram alarmes — Foto: Abraão Cruz/g1

articles.body: Vishal Chaturvedi’s 'Hanuman Ansh' recorded a slight increase in box office earnings on Tuesday, October 13. According to Sacnilk, the devotional drama collected Rs 1.30 cr net in India on Day 68, marking a 4% rise from Monday’s Rs 1.25 cr. The latest figures cover 2,951 shows across the Hindi and Telugu versions.The film’s cumulative India net collection has reached Rs 337.03 cr, while its domestic gross stands at Rs 397.80 cr. Overseas earnings added Rs 10 lakhs on Tuesday, taking the total overseas gross to Rs 40.60 cr. This brings the worldwide gross collection to Rs 438.40 cr.'Hanuman Ansh' records Rs 1.30 cr on Day 68The Hindi version contributed Rs 55 lakhs from 1,812 shows on its 68th day. Meanwhile, the Telugu version collected Rs 75 lakhs from 1,139 shows on its fifth day in theatres. The Telugu release arrived on October 9, while the Hindi version had premiered on August 7, 2026.The film recorded an overall occupancy of 17.2% across both language versions on Tuesday. Hindi screenings registered 16% occupancy, compared with 19% for the Telugu version. The reported footfalls for Day 68 stood at 134,624. Sacnilk’s overall verdict for the film remains blockbuster.Film’s weekly collections show strong mid-run growth'Hanuman Ansh' collected Rs 1.08 cr in its opening week, followed by Rs 40 lakhs in Week 2. Earnings improved to Rs 10.40 cr in Week 3 before reaching Rs 61.00 cr in Week 4. The film recorded its strongest weekly total in Week 5, collecting Rs 90.25 cr.The upward run continued with Rs 80.25 cr in Week 6. Its total for the week reached Rs 29.20 cr.Ninth and tenth weeks witness a changeDuring Week 9, 'Hanuman Ansh' collected Rs 10.60 cr. Wednesday and Thursday each brought in Rs 0.75 cr.The tenth week began with Rs 1.20 cr on Friday, October 9. Collections increased to Rs 2.50 cr on Saturday and Rs 2.80 cr on Sunday, before dropping to Rs 1.25 cr on Monday.
